propositions: Six src/rebar files sit within 20 LOC of the hard 800-LOC module-size cap with no other owner, creating a CI failure risk for any contributor who adds code or comments to them.

The module-size gate has no allowlist and the limit is locked, so any edit to a file at 799-800 LOC fails the build; this has already failed Gerrit 1916 when a six-line comment pushed __main__.py over the cap.

Splitting must follow existing logical concerns and architectural boundaries in the call graph, never be mechanical line-shaving, and must leave real headroom (target 200-500 LOC per file, no file under 100 LOC).
All splits must preserve behavior, pass unmodified tests, pass lint and typecheck, and update stale registries and line-budgets keyed to moved symbols.
_config_sources.py was recently left uncovered when in-flight work landed and closed, making it the only near-cap file with no owner beyond the original six.
Current census is stale after 45 recent changes added code to multiple src/rebar modules; the next session must re-measure before selecting extraction targets.
